content_html:
Parametric CAD for 3D printing. Runs on Linux, Windows and macOS.

SindriCAD is a history-based solid modeler. You sketch, extrude, fillet, and pattern your way to a part, and every step stays editable in a feature tree. It is not a mesh editor, and it is not a geometry kernel of its own. It drives build123d on top of OpenCASCADE for the actual geometry, and puts a real modeling UI and a print workflow on top.

It began on Linux, where good parametric CAD has always been thin on the ground, and it runs natively on all three desktops now: Linux, Windows and macOS. It is built for 3D printing: color a multi-material model, export it as a ready-to-slice OrcaSlicer project set up for the Snapmaker U1, and send the sliced G-code to the printer over the LAN.

Named for Sindri, the dwarven smith of Norse myth.

Status: beta, in ongoing development. SindriCAD already builds real printed parts, but the feature set is still filling out and rough edges remain. Expect frequent releases, report what breaks, and keep backups of documents you care about.

Get it

Installers for Linux, Windows and macOS are on the latest beta release, rebuilt automatically from every green main build. Free, no account needed, and everything is bundled including Python and the geometry engine. The builds are unsigned, so the first launch needs one extra step per platform: see Install for the exact steps. macOS is the awkward one: it refuses outright and claims the app is damaged, which it is not.

If SindriCAD looks useful, starring the repo helps other people find it.

What changed in each build is in CHANGELOG.md, and the same notes appear on the release itself.

What it does

  • Sketching with lines, arcs, circles, splines, rectangles, slots, polygons, and text in system fonts, plus associative patterns (bolt circles, grids, honeycomb) and a PlaneGCS constraint solver. Dimensions are entered on the canvas: type a value, press Tab to lock it, Enter to commit.
  • Parameters and expressions: name a value once, use it anywhere a number goes, and write arithmetic between parameters. Change one number and the whole part follows.
  • Features: Extrude (new body, join, cut, intersect, per region), Revolve, Loft, Sweep, Press/Pull (multi-face, and extrude up to a target surface), Fillet, Chamfer, Shell, Draft, Scale, Mirror, and patterns.
  • Offset Face and Thicken: push selected faces along their own normals with the surrounding walls following, or give surface geometry a wall. Thicken is what turns a non-watertight mesh import, which arrives as read-only reference geometry, into a solid you can actually model with.
  • Surface textures (see below).
  • Direct editing: Move with a live ghost preview, Split, Combine, Delete Face with automatic healing, and a cleanup pass for messy imported geometry.
  • Import STEP, BREP, STL, 3MF, OBJ, and GLB, with facet cleanup and STEP canonicalization, so imported parts come back as editable faces instead of a triangle soup. A STEP assembly keeps its tree: subassemblies and part names as the CAD system wrote them, each part still individually selectable. Export STEP, STL, 3MF, and GLB.
  • References that survive edits: geometry is picked by queryable descriptors (an axis, a face normal, the nearest point), never by a topology index. Change an upstream parameter and a downstream fillet still lands on the right edge.
  • Measure and section tools for checking a part before it prints.
  • A print pipeline for the Snapmaker U1 (see below).

Press ? in the app for the full keyboard shortcut list.


A part is its history: sketch, extrude, fillet, cut, texture, and every step stays editable.

Sketching

Sketches are constraint-driven. Dimensions are entered on the canvas: type a value, Tab to lock it, Enter to commit. A PlaneGCS solver keeps the rest of the profile consistent as you edit. Equal, parallel, perpendicular, concentric and the usual family of constraints render as glyphs you can click, and a reference dimension measures without driving. Conflicting and over-defined constraints are called out rather than silently ignored.

Surface textures

Textures turn a plain face into a tactile printed surface: knurling for grip, hexagon, rib or wave relief for looks, Voronoi and noise for organic breakup, or any grayscale image as a height map. Pick faces (or a whole body), set depth, scale, and angle, and the pattern is applied as real displaced geometry, not a shader trick: what you see is what the slicer gets.

The faceted patterns are built as exact lattices. Mesh vertices land on the pattern's own crease lines, so a knurl prints as crisp diamonds and a hexagon pattern as flat-topped cells with sharp walls, instead of the rounded mush a sampled height field gives. Patterns wrap around cylinders and cones: ribs and waves close on themselves at any angle, and the 2D lattices (knurl, hexagon) close at multiples of 90 degrees, which is geometry rather than a limitation to fix. Textures can also cut inward instead of embossing outward, and a two-tone mode prints the textured faces in a different palette color than the rest of the body.


Patterns wrap a full turn and meet themselves at the seam.

Inspect and measure

A section plane cuts the model live, so a shelled or hollow part can be checked from the inside before it prints. Drag the arrow along the axis, or type an exact offset.

Measure reports the true shortest distance between two faces or edges, not just their centres, along with the per-axis deltas, the centre-to-centre distance, and the angle between them.

Import and round-trip

STEP, BREP, STL, 3MF, OBJ, and GLB come in; STEP, STL, 3MF, and GLB go out. A STEP import arrives as real B-rep geometry. The faces above are ordinary selections on a body that was exported to STEP and read straight back in, so imported parts can be measured, sectioned, textured, and used as sketch planes instead of arriving as a triangle soup. Mesh formats are cleaned up on the way in, and STEP is canonicalized so its faces come back in a form the selectors can address.

A STEP file holding an assembly keeps its structure. The Browser shows the tree the originating CAD system wrote: subassemblies as collapsible groups, parts named as the file names them, and one entry per solid so a product like "M3 Nut (x20)" stays a single named group whose twenty pieces are still individually selectable. Two limits worth knowing up front: subassembly names come from the file and cannot be renamed in the Browser, and only STEP carries the tree back out so far, not 3MF or glTF. Part colours are read from the file and written back into an exported STEP, but not displayed on screen, because a body's colour here means which filament prints it.

Exporting to STEP preserves what import kept: the hierarchy, the part names, the colours and the position of every occurrence. Re-importing your own export returns the same parts, names, colours, positions and face count.

Snapmaker U1 print pipeline

SindriCAD carries print prep for the Snapmaker U1 multi-material printer from model to machine, so a colored parametric part reaches a print without a manual export dance.


Sketch text, extruded and mapped to its own filament slot.

  • Multi-material and multi-color 3MF: assign palette colors to bodies and export an OrcaSlicer project 3MF with per-object extruder (tool) mapping for the U1's tool changer (sidecar/project3mf.py).
  • Slicer handoff: "Open in OrcaSlicer" binds the U1 preset with your tuned process and filament, so you land ready to slice.
  • Direct device layer: a Rust Moonraker client (src-tauri/src/printer.rs) uploads G-code to the printer over the LAN with a filament-mapping dialog, reads the palette back from the printer, and monitors the running print.

U1 support will keep growing: I add features as I come up with them and have time for them.

Document format

A .sindri file is JSON: a parameter table and an ordered list of features.

Any numeric field is either a literal (5) or the name of a parameter ("width").


Change a parameter, the whole part follows, and the corner fillets stay on their edges.

Install

The geometry engine and its Python runtime are bundled, so those need no separate install. On Linux the app uses your distribution's WebKit rather than carrying its own, which is the one system dependency worth knowing about: see Requirements. The builds are unsigned for now, so the first launch needs one extra step per platform. Open the section for your platform:

Requirements

Needs
Linux (.deb, .rpm, AppImage) glibc 2.34 or newer, plus WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3 from your distribution
Windows Windows 10 or 11, x86-64. Edge WebView2, which the setup exe fetches if it is missing
macOS Apple Silicon. There is no Intel build yet

None of the Linux builds carry their own WebKit, the AppImage included. They use the one your distribution ships, which keeps them smaller and means they follow your distro's security updates instead of freezing a browser engine in place. The .deb and .rpm declare that dependency, so a package install pulls it in for you; an AppImage on a distribution without WebKitGTK 4.1 installed will need it added by hand.

Every platform needs working GPU drivers for the 3D viewport (OpenGL or EGL).

WebKit may log GStreamer element appsink not found. Nothing in modeling, export or printing uses it, so it is safe to ignore; installing your distribution's gst-plugins-base silences it.

Windows (.exe or .msi, self-updating)
  1. Download SindriCAD_<version>_x64-setup.exe (or the .msi) from the latest beta.
  2. The build is unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn "Windows protected your PC". Click "More info", then "Run anyway".

SindriCAD needs Microsoft Edge WebView2, which Windows 10 and 11 already ship; the setup exe fetches it automatically if it is missing. Once installed, SindriCAD updates itself: it checks the beta release at startup and offers a one-click restart-and-update.

Linux (.AppImage, .deb or .rpm)

Grab the .AppImage (chmod +x, updates itself in place), or the .deb / .rpm (sudo dpkg -i / sudo rpm -i; updates come from your package manager workflow, not in-app).

All three use your distribution's WebKitGTK 4.1 rather than carrying one, so a system that does not already have it needs it installed first. See Requirements.

macOS (.dmg, unsigned: one command on first launch)

SindriCAD is not signed with an Apple Developer certificate yet, so macOS quarantines it on download. It reports that as "SindriCAD.app is damaged and can't be opened. You should move it to the Trash." The download is not damaged. That is the message macOS shows for an app whose signature it cannot verify.

Drag the app to Applications, then clear the quarantine flag:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/SindriCAD.app

Adjust the path if you put it somewhere else. Alternatively, open System Settings, go to Privacy and Security, and choose Open Anyway after the first failed launch.

Right-clicking the app and choosing Open is the older advice and is not enough on current macOS, which is what this section used to say. Apple code signing is planned; it needs a paid Apple Developer account.

Builds are Apple Silicon only for now. An Intel Mac will fail for a different reason, and the command above will not help it.

3Dconnexion SpaceMouse (optional, one udev rule on Linux)

SindriCAD reads a SpaceMouse natively for 6DOF camera navigation, with the two buttons mapped to Fit and Home/ISO. Plug it in: no driver or configuration needed. Sensitivity and axis inversion live in Settings.

On Linux the device node (/dev/hidrawN) is root-only until a udev rule grants the logged-in user access. The .deb and .rpm packages install that rule for you and reload udev, so a packaged install just works.

The AppImage cannot install system files, so it needs the rule once, by hand:

sudo curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MakerViking/sindricad/main/packaging/99-spacemouse.rules -o /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/99-sindricad-spacemouse.rules
sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=hidraw

Building from a clone? Run sudo sh packaging/setup-spacemouse.sh instead. It installs the same rule and applies it to an already-connected device.

If SindriCAD can see the device but can't open it, it says so in a notification rather than failing silently. Two usual causes: the rule above is missing, or spacenavd / the official 3Dconnexion driver is already holding the device. Stop that service to let SindriCAD read it directly.

Build and run

Prerequisites: Node, a Rust toolchain, Python 3.12, uv, and WebKitGTK. See docs/PACKAGING.md for per-OS package names and known-good versions. A system OpenCASCADE install is not needed for the default build: the geometry sidecar ships its own OCCT inside its Python wheels. OCCT is only needed for the opt-in rust-geom Cargo feature (see docs/PACKAGING.md).

# 1. geometry sidecar (Python 3.12 via uv, locked versions from uv.lock)
cd sidecar
uv sync
uv run python test_smoke.py    # backend sanity (rebuild/export/error naming)
uv run python test_ws.py       # WebSocket transport sanity

# 2. the app, from the repo root. Tauri starts Vite and the sidecar for you.
npm install
npm run tauri dev

For frontend-only iteration you can run the two halves separately:

cd sidecar && uv run python server.py     # ws://127.0.0.1:8765
npm run dev                               # http://localhost:5173

Note: on Linux a standalone python server.py arms PR_SET_PDEATHSIG and dies with the shell that started it. To keep one alive across shells (or on other platforms), run it in a terminal you keep open, and kill it by hand when done or it will hold port 8765.

Architecture

┌─ Tauri shell (Rust) ──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  • native window, file dialogs                             │
│  • spawns and supervises the Python geometry sidecar       │
│  • kills the sidecar on app exit (process-group + PDEATHSIG)│
│                                                            │
│  ┌─ Frontend (TypeScript, in the webview) ──────────────┐  │
│  │  • Three.js viewport (orbit/pan/zoom, ViewCube,      │  │
│  │    picking, Z-up)                                    │  │
│  │  • UI: browser tree, timeline, parameters, toolbar   │  │
│  │  • owns the DOCUMENT (feature tree + parameters)     │  │
│  └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┘
                      │  JSON over localhost WebSocket (ws://127.0.0.1:8765)
                      ▼
┌─ Geometry sidecar (Python + build123d + OCCT) ────────────┐
│  • rebuild(document) -> mesh + per-triangle faceIds + edges │
│  • export(document, format, path) -> STEP / STL / 3MF       │
│  • selector resolution (topological-naming mitigation)     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Design decisions worth knowing up front:

  • Geometry lives only in Python on the shipping path. Rust never touches it there. There is an experimental opt-in Rust geometry path on OpenCASCADE, gated behind VITE_GEOM=rust, but a 2026 feasibility study found a Rust kernel could not beat OCCT on robustness or speed, so the Python build123d sidecar stays the default and the source of truth.
  • Full rebuild on every change. The frontend sends the whole document, the sidecar rebuilds from scratch and returns a fresh mesh. There is no server-side state.
  • The parametric engine is the build123d tree, re-run. Nothing more exotic.
  • Selectors, not indices. Geometry is referenced by queryable descriptors so references survive edits that renumber the underlying topology.

See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for the full invariant list and the rebuild pipeline, and docs/PROTOCOL.md for the sidecar's wire protocol.

Project layout

sidecar/      build123d geometry service (builder, geom_select, tessellate, exporters, server)
src/          frontend: viewport/, ui/, document/, geometry/, input/, io/, print/
src-tauri/    Rust shell: lib.rs (entry), sidecar.rs (lifecycle), printer.rs (U1 device layer)

License

SindriCAD is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0-only), see LICENSE. AGPL's network copyleft means any fork, or any modified version offered over a network, has to publish its source under the same terms.

Contributions are welcome under CONTRIBUTING.md, which includes a short contributor agreement so the project can stay open under the AGPL while the maintainer can also offer commercial terms to those who need them. Third-party components and their licenses are listed in NOTICE.md.

Support

SindriCAD is free and open source. If it earns a place in your workflow, you can back development on Patreon (MuninWorks). Patronage covers the servers, domains, and tooling behind this and my other projects.

Architecture ┌─ Tauri shell (Rust) ──────────────────────────────────────┐ │ • native window, file dialogs │ │ • spawns and supervises the Python geometry sidecar │ │ • kills the sidecar on app exit (process-group + PDEATHSIG)│ │ │ │ ┌─ Frontend (TypeScript, in the webview) ──────────────┐ │ │ │ • Three.js viewport (orbit/pan/zoom, ViewCube, │ │ │ │ picking, Z-up) │ │ │ │ • UI: browser tree, timeline, parameters, toolbar │ │ │ │ • owns the DOCUMENT (feature tree + parameters) │ │ │ └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘ │ └─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┘ │ JSON over localhost WebSocket (ws://127.0.0.1:8765) ▼ ┌─ Geometry sidecar (Python + build123d + OCCT) ────────────┐ │ • rebuild(document) -> mesh + per-triangle faceIds + edges │ │ • export(document, format, path) -> STEP / STL / 3MF │ │ • selector resolution (topological-naming mitigation) │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Design decisions worth knowing up front: Geometry lives only in Python on the shipping path. Rust never touches it there. There is an experimental opt-in Rust geometry path on OpenCASCADE, gated behind VITE_GEOM=rust, but a 2026 feasibility study found a Rust kernel could not beat OCCT on robustness or speed, so the Python build123d sidecar stays the default and the source of truth. Full rebuild on every change. The frontend sends the whole document, the sidecar rebuilds from scratch and returns a fresh mesh. There is no server-side state. The parametric engine is the build123d tree, re-run. Nothing more exotic. Selectors, not indices. Geometry is referenced by queryable descriptors so references survive edits that renumber the underlying topology. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for the full invariant list and the rebuild pipeline, and docs/PROTOCOL.md for the sidecar's wire protocol. Project layout sidecar/ build123d geometry service (builder, geom_select, tessellate, exporters, server) src/ frontend: viewport/, ui/, document/, geometry/, input/, io/, print/ src-tauri/ Rust shell: lib.rs (entry), sidecar.rs (lifecycle), printer.rs (U1 device layer) License SindriCAD is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0-only), see LICENSE. blocks.html_en: Textures turn a plain face into a tactile printed surface: knurling for grip, hexagon, rib or wave relief for looks, Voronoi and noise for organic breakup, or any grayscale image as a height map. Pick faces (or a whole body), set depth, scale, and angle, and the pattern is applied as real displaced geometry, not a shader trick: what you see is what the slicer gets.

blocks.html_en: The faceted patterns are built as exact lattices. Mesh vertices land on the pattern's own crease lines, so a knurl prints as crisp diamonds and a hexagon pattern as flat-topped cells with sharp walls, instead of the rounded mush a sampled height field gives. Patterns wrap around cylinders and cones: ribs and waves close on themselves at any angle, and the 2D lattices (knurl, hexagon) close at multiples of 90 degrees, which is geometry rather than a limitation to fix. Textures can also cut inward instead of embossing outward, and a two-tone mode prints the textured faces in a different palette color than the rest of the body.

blocks.html_en: STEP, BREP, STL, 3MF, OBJ, and GLB come in; STEP, STL, 3MF, and GLB go out. A STEP import arrives as real B-rep geometry. The faces above are ordinary selections on a body that was exported to STEP and read straight back in, so imported parts can be measured, sectioned, textured, and used as sketch planes instead of arriving as a triangle soup. Mesh formats are cleaned up on the way in, and STEP is canonicalized so its faces come back in a form the selectors can address.

blocks.html_en: A STEP file holding an assembly keeps its structure. The Browser shows the tree the originating CAD system wrote: subassemblies as collapsible groups, parts named as the file names them, and one entry per solid so a product like "M3 Nut (x20)" stays a single named group whose twenty pieces are still individually selectable. Part colours are read from the file and written back into an exported STEP, but not displayed on screen, because a body's colour here means which filament prints it.

content_html_zh:
用于 3D 打印的参数化 CAD。 可在 Linux、Windows 和 macOS 上运行。

SindriCAD 是一个基于历史的实体建模器。 您可以按照自己的方式绘制草图、拉伸、圆角和图案化零件，并且每一步都在特征树中保持可编辑状态。 它不是一个网格编辑器，也不是它自己的几何内核。 它在 OpenCASCADE 之上驱动 build123d 以实现实际几何形状，并在顶部放置真实的建模 UI 和打印工作流程。

它始于 Linux，良好的参数化 CAD 一直很少见，现在它可以在所有三个桌面上本机运行：Linux、Windows 和 macOS。 它专为 3D 打印而设计：为多材料模型着色，将其导出为为 Snapmaker U1 设置的可切片 OrcaSlicer 项目，并通过 LAN 将切片的 G 代码发送到打印机。

以北欧神话中的矮人铁匠辛德里 (Sindri) 命名。

状态：测试版，正在开发中。 SindriCAD 已经构建了真正的打印零件，但功能集仍在填充中，并且仍然存在粗糙的边缘。 期待频繁的发布，报告出现的问题，并保留您关心的文档的备份。

获取它 · 它的作用 · 绘制草图 · 纹理 · 测量 · 导入 · 打印管道 · 文档格式 安装 · 构建和运行 · 架构 · 项目布局 · 许可证 · 支持 · 更改日志

Get it

Linux、Windows 和 macOS 的安装程序采用最新的测试版本，从每个绿色主版本自动重建。 免费，无需帐户，并且所有内容都捆绑在一起，包括 Python 和几何引擎。 构建未签名，因此第一次启动每个平台都需要一个额外的步骤：请参阅安装以了解确切的步骤。 macOS 是一个尴尬的问题：它直接拒绝并声称应用程序已损坏，但事实并非如此。

如果 SindriCAD 看起来有用，为该存储库添加星标可以帮助其他人找到它。

每个版本中发生的更改都在 CHANGELOG.md 中，并且相同的注释出现在版本本身上。

它的作用

  • 使用系统字体中的直线、圆弧、圆、样条线、矩形、槽、多边形和文本以及关联图案（螺栓圆、网格、蜂窝）和 PlaneGCS 约束解算器进行草图绘制。 在画布上输入尺寸：输入一个值，按 Tab 键锁定它，按 Enter 键提交。
  • 参数和表达式：一次命名一个值，在任何数字所在的地方使用它，并在参数之间编写算术。 改变一个数字，整个部分就随之而来。
  • 功能：拉伸（新体、连接、剪切、相交、每个区域）、旋转、放样、扫描、按/拉（多面和拉伸到目标曲面）、圆角、倒角、抽壳、拔模、缩放、镜像和图案。
  • 偏移面和加厚：沿着其自身的法线推动选定的面，周围的墙跟随其后，或为曲面几何体提供墙。 加厚可以将非防水网格导入（作为只读参考几何体到达）转变为您可以实际建模的实体。
  • 表面纹理（见下文）。
  • 直接编辑：使用实时重影预览移动、分割、合并、删除面并自动修复，以及清理杂乱的导入几何体。
  • 导入 STEP、BREP、STL、3MF、OBJ 和 GLB，并进行面清理和 STEP 标准化，因此导入的零件会以可编辑面而不是三角形形式返回。 STEP 装配体保留其树：子装配体和零件名称与 CAD 系统编写的一样，每个零件仍然可以单独选择。 导出 STEP、STL、3MF 和 GLB。
  • 编辑后仍然存在的引用：几何体是通过可查询的描述符（轴、面法线、最近的点）选取的，而不是通过拓扑索引选取的。 更改上游参数，下游圆角仍然位于右边缘。
  • 用于在打印之前检查零件的测量和剖切工具。
  • Snapmaker U1 的打印管道（见下文）。

按 ？ 在应用程序中查看完整的键盘快捷键列表。

零件就是它的历史：草图、拉伸、圆角、切割、纹理，每一步都保持可编辑。

素描

草图是约束驱动的。 在画布上输入尺寸：输入一个值，按 Tab 锁定它，按 Enter 提交。 PlaneGCS 解算器在您编辑时使轮廓的其余部分保持一致。 相等、平行、垂直、同心和常见的约束系列呈现为您可以单击的字形，并且无需驾驶即可测量参考尺寸。 冲突的和过度定义的约束会被指出，而不是默默地被忽略。

表面纹理

纹理将普通的脸变成有触觉的印刷表面：滚花用于抓握，六边形、肋骨或波浪浮雕用于外观，Voronoi 和噪声用于有机分解，或任何灰度图像作为高度图。 选取面（或整个身体），设置深度、比例和角度，并将图案应用为真实的位移几何体，而不是着色器技巧：您所看到的就是切片器得到的。

多面图案被构建为精确的格子。 网格顶点落在图案自己的折痕线上，因此滚花打印为清晰的菱形，六边形图案打印为带有尖锐壁的平顶单元，而不是采样高度字段给出的圆形糊状。 图案环绕圆柱体和圆锥体：肋条和波浪以任何角度自行闭合，二维晶格（滚花、六边形）以 90 度的倍数闭合，这是几何学而不是需要修复的限制。 纹理也可以向内切割而不是向外浮雕，并且双色调模式以与身体其他部分不同的调色板颜色打印纹理面。

图案环绕一整圈并在接缝处相遇。

检查和测量

剖面可以实时切割模型，因此可以在打印之前从内部检查带壳或空心零件。 沿轴拖动箭头，或输入精确的偏移量。

测量报告两个面或边缘之间的真实最短距离（而不仅仅是它们的中心），以及每轴增量、中心到中心的距离以及它们之间的角度。

进口及往返

STEP、BREP、STL、3MF、OBJ 和 GLB 登场； STEP、STL、3MF、GLB 熄灭。 STEP 导入作为真实的 B-rep 几何体到达。 上面的面是导出到 STEP 并直接读回的实体上的普通选择，因此可以对导入的零件进行测量、剖切、纹理化并用作草图平面，而不是作为三角形汤。 网格格式在传入过程中被清理，STEP 被规范化，因此它的面以选择器可以寻址的形式返回。

保存程序集的 STEP 文件会保留其结构。 浏览器显示原始 CAD 系统编写的树：作为可折叠组的子装配体、按照文件名命名的零件以及每个实体一个条目，因此像“M3 Nut (x20)”这样的产品仍保留为单个命名组，其 20 个部件仍可单独选择。 值得预先了解的两个限制：子装配体名称来自文件，无法在浏览器中重命名，并且到目前为止只有 STEP 将树带回，3MF 或 glTF 则不然。 零件颜色从文件中读取并写回到导出的 STEP 中，但不会显示在屏幕上，因为此处主体的颜色意味着哪个灯丝打印它。

导出到 STEP 会保留导入时保留的内容：层次结构、零件名称、颜色和每次出现的位置。 重新导入您自己的导出会返回相同的零件、名称、颜色、位置和面数。

Snapmaker U1 打印管道

SindriCAD 为 Snapmaker U1 多材料打印机从模型到机器进行打印准备，因此彩色参数零件无需手动导出即可实现打印。

草图文本，挤出并映射到其自己的灯丝槽。

  • 多材料和多颜色 3MF：将调色板颜色分配给实体，并导出 OrcaSlicer 项目 3MF，其中包含用于 U1 工具更换器的每个对象挤出机（工具）映射 (sidecar/project3mf.py)。
  • 切片器交接：“在 OrcaSlicer 中打开”将 U1 预设与您调整的流程和灯丝绑定在一起，以便您做好切片准备。
  • 直接设备层：Rust Moonraker 客户端 (src-tauri/src/printer.rs) 使用灯丝映射对话框通过 LAN 将 G 代码上传到打印机，从打印机读回调色板，并监视正在运行的打印。

U1 支持将不断增长：我会在想出新功能时添加它们，并且有时间使用它们。

文件格式

.sindri 文件是 JSON：参数表和有序的功能列表。

任何数字字段要么是文字 (5)，要么是参数名称（“宽度”）。

更改参数，整个零件都会跟随，并且角圆角保留在其边缘上。

安装

几何引擎及其 Python 运行时是捆绑在一起的，因此不需要单独安装。 在 Linux 上，应用程序使用您的发行版的 WebKit，而不是自带它自己的 WebKit，这是值得了解的一个系统依赖项：请参阅要求。 目前构建尚未签名，因此第一次启动需要每个平台执行一个额外的步骤。 打开适合您的平台的部分：

要求

Needs
Linux（.deb、.rpm、AppImage） glibc 2.34 或更高版本，以及您的发行版中的 WebKitGTK 4.1 和 GTK 3
视窗 Windows 10 或 11，x86-64。 Edge WebView2，安装程序 exe 在丢失时会获取它
macOS 苹果硅。 目前还没有英特尔版本

所有 Linux 版本都没有自带 WebKit，包括 AppImage。 他们使用您的发行版附带的版本，这使得它们更小，并且意味着他们遵循您的发行版的安全更新，而不是冻结浏览器引擎。 .deb 和 .rpm 声明了该依赖关系，因此软件包安装会为您拉取它；未安装 WebKitGTK 4.1 的发行版上的 AppImage 需要手动添加。

每个平台都需要适用于 3D 视口（OpenGL 或 EGL）的有效 GPU 驱动程序。

WebKit 可能会记录未找到 GStreamer 元素 appsink。 建模、导出或打印中没有任何内容使用它，因此可以放心地忽略它；安装发行版的 gst-plugins-base 会使其静音。

Windows (.exe or .msi, self-updating)
  1. 从最新测试版下载 SindriCAD_<版本>_x64-setup.exe（或 .msi）。
  2. 该版本未签名，因此 SmartScreen 将警告“Windows 保护了您的电脑”。 单击“更多信息”，然后单击“仍然运行”。

SindriCAD 需要 Microsoft Edge WebView2，Windows 10 和 11 已提供该功能；如果丢失，安装程序 exe 会自动获取它。 安装后，SindriCAD 会自行更新：它会在启动时检查测试版本并提供一键式重新启动和更新。

Linux (.AppImage, .deb or .rpm)

获取 .AppImage（chmod +x，就地更新自身）或 .deb / .rpm（sudo dpkg -i / sudo rpm -i；更新来自包管理器工作流程，而不是应用程序内）。

所有三个都使用您的发行版的 WebKitGTK 4.1，而不是自带一个，因此尚未安装它的系统需要先安装它。 请参阅要求。

macOS (.dmg, unsigned: one command on first launch)

SindriCAD 尚未使用 Apple 开发者证书进行签名，因此 macOS 在下载时将其隔离。 它报告说“SindriCAD.app 已损坏且无法打开。 你应该将其移至垃圾箱。” 下载的文件没有损坏。 这是 macOS 针对无法验证签名的应用程序显示的消息。

将应用程序拖到应用程序，然后清除隔离标志：

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/SindriCAD.app

如果你把它放在其他地方，请调整路径。 或者，打开“系统设置”，转到“隐私和安全”，然后在第一次启动失败后选择“仍然打开”。

右键单击应用程序并选择“打开”是较旧的建议，在当前的 macOS 上还不够，这就是本节所说的内容。 Apple 代码签名已计划；它需要一个付费的苹果开发者帐户。

目前仅使用 Apple Silicon 进行构建。 Intel Mac 会因不同的原因而失败，上面的命令无济于事。

3Dconnexion SpaceMouse (optional, one udev rule on Linux)

SindriCAD 本身读取 SpaceMouse 以进行 6DOF 相机导航，其中两个按钮映射到 Fit 和 Home/ISO。 插入即可：无需驱动程序或配置。 灵敏度和轴反转位于“设置”中。

在 Linux 上，设备节点 (/dev/hidrawN) 仅限 root，直到 udev 规则授予登录用户访问权限。 .deb 和 .rpm 软件包会为您安装该规则并重新加载 udev，因此打包安装即可正常工作。

AppImage 无法安装系统文件，因此需要手动执行一次规则：

sudo curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MakerViking/sindricad/main/packaging/99-spacemouse.rules -o /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/99-sindricad-spacemouse.rules
sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=hidraw

从克隆构建？ 改为运行 sudo sh Packaging/setup-spacemouse.sh。 它安装相同的规则并将其应用到已连接的设备。

如果 SindriCAD 可以看到该设备但无法打开它，它会在通知中进行说明，而不是默默地失败。 两个常见原因：缺少上述规则，或者 spacenavd / 官方 3Dconnexion 驱动程序已持有该设备。 停止该服务以让 SindriCAD 直接读取它。

构建并运行

先决条件：Node、Rust 工具链、Python 3.12、uv 和 WebKitGTK。 请参阅 docs/PACKAGING.md 了解每个操作系统的软件包名称和已知良好版本。 默认构建不需要系统 OpenCASCADE 安装：几何边车在其 Python 轮子内提供了自己的 OCCT。 仅选择加入 rust-geom Cargo 功能才需要 OCCT（请参阅 docs/PACKAGING.md）。

# 1. geometry sidecar (Python 3.12 via uv, locked versions from uv.lock)
cd sidecar
uv sync
uv run python test_smoke.py    # backend sanity (rebuild/export/error naming)
uv run python test_ws.py       # WebSocket transport sanity

# 2. the app, from the repo root. Tauri starts Vite and the sidecar for you.
npm install
npm run tauri dev

对于仅前端迭代，您可以分别运行两半：

cd sidecar && uv run python server.py     # ws://127.0.0.1:8765
npm run dev                               # http://localhost:5173
注意：在 Linux 上，独立的 python server.py 配备 PR_SET_PDEATHSIG 并随启动它的 shell 一起终止。 要使一个跨 shell（或在其他平台上）保持活动状态，请在保持打开的终端中运行它，并在完成后手动终止它，否则它将占用端口 8765。

建筑学

┌─ Tauri shell (Rust) ──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  • native window, file dialogs                             │
│  • spawns and supervises the Python geometry sidecar       │
│  • kills the sidecar on app exit (process-group + PDEATHSIG)│
│                                                            │
│  ┌─ Frontend (TypeScript, in the webview) ──────────────┐  │
│  │  • Three.js viewport (orbit/pan/zoom, ViewCube,      │  │
│  │    picking, Z-up)                                    │  │
│  │  • UI: browser tree, timeline, parameters, toolbar   │  │
│  │  • owns the DOCUMENT (feature tree + parameters)     │  │
│  └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┘
                      │  JSON over localhost WebSocket (ws://127.0.0.1:8765)
                      ▼
┌─ Geometry sidecar (Python + build123d + OCCT) ────────────┐
│  • rebuild(document) -> mesh + per-triangle faceIds + edges │
│  • export(document, format, path) -> STEP / STL / 3MF       │
│  • selector resolution (topological-naming mitigation)     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

值得预先了解的设计决策：

  • 几何只存在于Python 的运输路径中。 铁锈永远不会触及那里。 OpenCASCADE 上有一个实验性的选择加入 Rust 几何路径，位于 VITE_GEOM=rust 后面，但 2026 年的可行性研究发现 Rust 内核无法在鲁棒性或速度上击败 OCCT，因此 Python build123d sidecar 仍然是默认值和事实来源。
  • 每次更改都完全重建。 前端发送整个文档，sidecar 从头开始​​重建并返回一个新的网格。 没有服务器端状态。
  • 参数引擎是build123d树，重新运行。 没有什么更异国情调的了。
  • 选择器，而不是索引。 几何图形由可查询描述符引用，因此引用可以在对基础拓扑重新编号的编辑后继续存在。

请参阅 docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 了解完整的不变列表和重建管道，以及 docs/PROTOCOL.md 了解 sidecar 的线路协议。

项目布局
